Common.Rule: Standing up costs you no action (you still get the half Move)
When you would be made Shook or Flustered, you may spend your reaction to ignore it
Locked doors and windows do not stop your movement: you know the cat flap. They still block sight
While you are downed, enemies cannot capture you: nobody can find you. You know where to hide
Your Assist reaches an ally within 6 inches, through walls, and every time you Assist you are **Announced**
Once an activation, swapping places with an ally costs you no action
Swapping what is in your hands costs you no action
While you are prone, a shooter loses one more die against you (2 in all)
When an ally within 3 inches Asks the voice, after the roll you may shout over it: nothing happens, whatever the result, and you are **Flustered**

Fight.Rule: You can Parry and Riposte (section 7.4). Needs a melee weapon
Your melee attacks against an enemy who already has a lasting condition have +1 die
The outnumbering dice enemies gain against you are reduced by 1
After you win a melee exchange you may, instead of Press, make the loser **Flustered**
After you win a melee exchange you may, instead of Press, knock the loser prone
When an ally in base contact with you is attacked in melee, you may spend your reaction to be attacked instead
You capture a downed enemy without the opposed roll if no other enemy is within 3 inches of you
An enemy who moves out of base contact with you is **Flustered** (you may still take a parting blow)

Shoot.Rule: Your Aim also ignores the target's light cover
A shot of yours that totals exactly 6 still makes the target **Flustered**
When an enemy grenade lands within 2 inches of you, you may spend your reaction to throw it back before it goes off: it scatters again, from you, toward a point of your choice within 8 inches
An Attack action with a gun, with no roll: an enemy in range and line of sight is **Flustered**. It counts as an attack for the second-attack rule and spends Energy as a shot would
Your shots ignore the "target moved" penalty
Clearing a jam on your own gear needs no test (it is still a Use action)
If you have not moved this round, you may spend your reaction to shoot an enemy who ends a Move action in your range and line of sight, at -1 die

Grit.Rule: You carry a downed ally alone at full Move
When a glance would give you a lasting condition, you may spend your reaction to ignore it
You need no Grit test to climb up or down a height of up to your Move, or to jump a gap you have the Move for. The Move cost is as usual
A Use action and a Routine (6) Grit test clear Winded from yourself
You pass Cold and Dangerous terrain tests without rolling
Your falls count as 3 inches shorter, and you land on your feet, not prone
Every height you climb up or down, and every ladder, counts as half as tall (rounded up) when you pay Move for it or compare it with your Move. A fall still uses the real height
One Winded does not count toward going down for you (a second Winded does)
When you spend both actions on Move, nobody may take a parting blow on you

Nerve.Rule: A Use action and a Routine (6) Nerve test: an ally in contact clears Winded or Flustered
If you have the gift, you may spend your reaction to ignore a madness result
The Nerve test your boast forces is Tricky (8) instead of Routine
An ally within 3 inches may use your Nerve instead of their own on a Nerve test
Enemy fighters' effects cannot make you **Flustered**
When you choose Take it against a shot and are still standing after it, you are **Hyped**
When you pass a Nerve test, one ally within 3 inches is **Hyped**
If you have the gift, your powers reach through one wall, as if the target were Announced

Tech.Rule: You may Recite (asking a voice first, section 8.1), you know one rite of your choice, and you can use its relics (section 8.3)

Tech.Advance: **Rite of Quiet, Light, Ward, Wrath, Calling or Mending** (needs Rites)
Tech.Rule: You know that rite as well, and can use its relics (section 8.3). Take it once for each rite
You can Patch up without a kit, at Tricky (8)
When your know-how test fails, roll twice on the weird table and choose
When your Counter-prompt makes a prompt fail, the machine takes the prompter literally: they roll on their crew's voice table, and only a bad result happens
You may Ask the voice after your roll instead of before, once you have seen the dice. Its result still applies to that roll
Your field patching also clears one jam on the patched fighter's gear
A Use action in base contact with an ally: move up to 2 Energy from your battery to theirs, or from theirs to yours
You may prompt a machine out of sight if an ally is in base contact with it, holding up the slate
